full_judgment: 14. The object of Rule 31 of Order 41 of the Code of Civil Procedure is to see that the appellate Court does not act mechanically in concurring with the findings of the trial Court. It requires that the appellate Court must discuss and consider the material evidence on record and come to its independent conclusions on all points at issue on the basis of the evidence. The appellate Court is also required to set aside the material findings of the trial Court with reference to the evidence on record adverting to the reasons assigned by it. In the case of a affirmance general agreement of the appellate Court with the findings of the trial Court may be considered sufficient but in case of reversal the discussion of evidence must necessarily be fairly elaborate. In our case under review, it is found that the learned trial Court while dismissing the suit record clear findings on all relevant points concerning the merit of the case and these are well-reasoned and well supported by the evidence on record. The learned Court on appeal below hopelessly filed to address itself in these material findings with reference to the evidence on record and thereby fell in error in passing the impugned Judgment on hypothetical considerations occasioning failure of justice.
